title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in this third draft of 'Analysis situs' (1986), Grothendieck is trying to axiomatize 'ateliers' or 'atlases'. These are collections M of 'figures', i.e. stratified pieces such as closed simplices or cells. They carry an order ≤ (being a sub-figure or face), a relation ≪ (being contained in, as a strict or closed sub-figure), and a disjointness relation ‖. The aim is a combinatorial, model-independent foundation for tame topology, in the spirit of Esquisse §5.

On the previous page he observed a flaw. If ≪ between simplices is just set-theoretic inclusion of closed sets, then a 1-simplex embedded as a curved arc inside a 2-simplex counts as a sub-figure. That would allow 'subdivisions' of Δ² into two curvilinear triangles, which no one would accept as simplicial. Classical practice is guided by the rigidity of affine simplices.

On this page he corrects his earlier notes ('GP V', pp. 19-20) accordingly. For the strict relation F ≪_s G between figures F and G (each a stratified set, i.e. a family of strata) he already had condition a): for every stratum A ∈ F, the set G^A of strata of G containing A has a smallest element. He now adds a second requirement. For every A ∈ F and B ∈ G, the intersection A∩B must be either empty or a sub-stratum (face) of A.

A crossed-out attempt rephrased this through the family induced by G on |F|: the traces on |F| of those B with B° ∩ |F| ≠ ∅.

He then says the compatibility criterion needs the same kind of tightening, into a 'strict' or 'polyhedral' compatibility. This requires not merely that the underlying set-theoretic figures of F and G be compatible, but that together they form polyhedral set-theoretic figures, so that intersections of strata are again strata.

Summary point: the 'special' axioms must be split into two kinds:
- those for 'polyhedral ateliers';
- those for 'special ateliers'.

He also warns that 'polyhedral set-theoretic ateliers' must not be confused with 'set-theoretic polyhedral ateliers', which are not ateliers at all.

For the eventual embedding of a polyhedral atelier into Fig(L), the figures of some ambient model L, one must require: Ensemb(F) ≪_pol Ensemb(G) ⟹ F ≪ G. In words, polyhedral containment of the underlying set-theoretic figures forces containment in the atelier. A margin note refers to a replacement at GP VI p.52.

This leads directly to the next page's definition of 'polyidéal' posets. These are posets in which two elements with a common lower bound have an infimum. A figure or atlas is polyidéal when two non-disjoint strata meet in a stratum; this is the combinatorial shadow of the condition introduced here.
errors: No outright mathematical error. This is a self-correction of earlier notes: the earlier criterion for F ≪_s G was too weak, since it admitted curvilinear 'subdivisions'.

The intersection condition 'A∩B empty or a sub-stratum of A' is not symmetric as stated. One would expect it also to need to be a sub-stratum of B, or at least a union of strata of B, for a genuinely polyhedral compatibility. On its own it still does not exclude all non-PL phenomena, e.g. wild or curved embeddings whose stratum-intersection pattern happens to be correct. The text does not address this.

ideas.what: Strengthening subfigure/refinement relations by requiring that pairwise intersections of strata be empty or a face (closed under intersection), to exclude non-rectilinear 'subdivisions'
ideas.modern_name: intersection condition for simplicial/polyhedral complexes; regular CW complexes / face posets closed under meets
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical PL topology (Whitehead, Alexander, Newman; standard in Rourke–Sanderson, Hudson)
ideas.where_published: Only the general tame-topology program appears in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6; the 'atelier' axiomatics are unpublished

ideas.what: Distinction between 'polyhedral ateliers' and 'special ateliers', and between 'polyhedral set-theoretic' and 'set-theoretic polyhedral' ateliers, in an axiomatics of stratified figures
ideas.modern_name: axiomatic tame topology / combinatorial stratified spaces (cf. o-minimal structures, poset-stratified spaces)
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight; stratified spaces: Thom, Mather, later Lurie, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka

ideas.what: Embedding axiom into Fig(L): polyhedral containment of the underlying set-theoretic figures implies containment in the atelier
ideas.modern_name: faithfulness/fullness condition for a realization functor to PL figures

missed.claim: The program of axiomatizing tame topology by order-theoretic data (M, ≤, ≪, ‖) on figures, with separate polyhedral and 'special' axiom systems and realization in Fig(L), was never completed or published. On this page he identifies set-theoretic incidence alone as insufficient to recover PL structure.
missed.quote: En résumé, pour la formulation des axiomes spéciaux, il faut distinguer ceux relatifs aux "ateliers polyédraux", et ceux relatifs aux "ateliers spéciaux".
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could be compared with modern combinatorial models of stratified spaces (exit-path categories, poset-stratified spaces, o-minimal triangulation). However, the specific content on this page is close to standard PL folklore.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working-correction page inside an unpublished axiomatics. Its mathematical content (strata intersections must be faces, so that curvilinear 'subdivisions' are excluded) is classical. Only the overall atelier program is of historical interest.

First line probably ends 'Améliorer' underlined, after 'ici le critère de v[érification?]'; uncertain.
